data.note: No replicates: one complete loading scan is the analysis unit. The four points are NOT independent replicates of anything.

model_table.shape: flat up to Lk then linear decline

indistinguishable_sets.by_aicc_note: AICc = AIC + 2k(k+1)/(n-k-1) is undefined for k=3 when n=4 (denominator zero); the finite-AICc ranking therefore contains only k<=2 models, all of which are monotone.

peak_location.bound_derivation: For a continuous single-peaked curve: rate(1.0) > rate(0.2) forces mode > 0.2; rate(1.0) > rate(3.0) forces mode < 3.0. Any mode in (0.2, 3.0) is consistent with the four values.

axis_sensitivity.note: The isotonic (PAVA) fits are the minimum-RSS fits over ALL monotone functions of L. Under any strictly increasing reparametrisation h(L) (log included) the ordering of the four points is unchanged, so the isotonic RSS is also the best monotone fit on the transformed axis: no monotone axis rescaling can remove the interior peak.

permutation_tests.note: n=4 -> exact permutation p-values; the smallest attainable two-sided p for a monotone association is 1/3.

limitations: n = 4 points, no replicates, no independent error estimate, residual df = 1 for any 3-parameter model: the noise level is not estimable from these data.
AICc is undefined for k=3 at n=4 (n-k-1 = 0). AICc cannot rank the flexible, peaked descriptions; any AICc-based conclusion here is an artefact of the denominator, not evidence.
With 3 parameters and 4 points, several families can interpolate the data exactly (RSS ~ 0), so AIC -> -infinity and the comparison is degenerate.
The four points carry 4 numbers; they cannot distinguish among all shapes that pass near those four numbers.
